OUR PEOPLE


Nov. 19, 2026


# The 20+ Club: Geew Jaggernauth


A series spotlighting Medline employees who have been with the company 20 years or longer


*This profile also appears in the Fall 2026 edition of* Medlines *, an in-house newsletter for Medline employees.*


##### Name: Geew Jaggernauth
Title: Receiving clerk, C05 distribution center
Current location: Auburndale, Fla.
Started with Medline: 2003


**BUSY FROM THE BEGINNING:** “My official start date was May 23 at our old distribution center in Orlando, but I started before that in January through a temp agency. A friend of mine who works here recommended me. I had worked for Brooks Brothers and for 14 years part-time at the Home Depot. For my first role with Medline, my supervisor was in the office handling paperwork, so I was in charge of the actual shipping in the shipping department. The director and I were the last people to leave the building each day.”


**MERRY MENTOR:** “From shipping, I migrated to receiving. The processes have gotten easier and made a difference in how quickly we can get products into the building and into stock so we can get them to the customer. We have some good people in receiving who I enjoy working with — newer people who don’t have the experience I do, so I teach them the ways I do things, the ins and outs. They treat me with a lot of respect because I’ve been here so long. I enjoy being in this role, to be honest. I’ve been offered higher positions, but I’m 58, and I’d rather somebody younger take those and move ahead, growing the company.”


**EAGLE EYES:** “I remember one time in Orlando, we had a couple of boxes come in that weren’t the item the vendor was supposed to send. I figured it out because the color on the box was different — it was supposed to be green, but it was a lighter green. I’d already been doing this so long, I could look at a box and know if something was wrong just by passing by and seeing the label. You memorize a lot. If I needed to, I could unload a trailer of incontinence briefs without looking at the paperwork or my labels, just knowing the numbers on the boxes.”


**WHAT MEDLINE HAS TAUGHT ME:** “How to deal with people. Everyone is different, and you have to educate yourself on how they react when you say something. I’m a people person, so I’ve learned how to get into a conversation with many different kinds of people.”


**HOME PLATE AND HOME REPAIR:** “Outside of work, the No. 1 thing for me now is taking care of my wife, but until a couple of years ago, I played softball as a catcher. I also have three rental properties, which I maintain myself. It’s going to be 30 years that I’ve been doing that. Before coming to Florida, I used to live in New York and had an eight-family apartment building.”


**BACK-POCKET SKILLS:** “I’m originally from Guyana. I was an apprentice welder for six months and then did high-pressure pipe welding for the Bauxide mining company before I immigrated. I still have all my certificates and a welding machine at home and will help whenever somebody needs some welding done at their house.”


**NO BETTER PLACE:** “I’ve worked in warehouses from 1987 to now — 39 years. I stick with Medline because Medline has been very good to me, very good to my family. I don’t see myself leaving until I’m ready to retire. I still look forward to coming to work every day.”
